implement.approach: Defect on BASE_SHA: apps/mobile/src/navigation/RootNavigator.tsx:534 `if (!navigationRef.isReady()) return;` drops any press before the container is ready; apps/mobile/src/notifications/service.ts:159-177 navigates immediately for both the cold-start read and foreground PRESS with no queue/dedupe; service.ts:184-189 registerBackgroundNotificationHandler only acknowledges events, although react-native-notify-kit (README + ios/RNNotifee/NotifeeApiModule.mm) delivers taps made while the app is inactive/suspended on the background channel — and RootNavigator mounts late (App.tsx renders it only after splash+auth+profile), so cold-start taps arrive before anything subscribes. Fix: (1) service.ts — exported `MAX_QUEUED_NOTIFICATION_PRESSES` (4) and generic `enqueueBounded()` (dedupe: repeat moves to newest slot; oldest dropped past the limit); a process-wide `pressIntake` {sink, pending, routedIds}: the foreground listener, the background handler and the cold-start read all go through it; presses with no subscriber wait in `pending` and are flushed when `subscribeToNotificationPresses` is called; PRESS notification ids are remembered (bounded) so `getInitialNotification()` of the same tap is not dispatched a second time; unsubscribe clears the sink only if it is still ours. (2) RootNavigator.tsx — presses seen while `!isReady()` are held in a bounded deduped ref queue and replayed once by `NotificationPressReplay`, a null-rendering child placed after the root navigator inside the container: its effect runs in the commit that registers the navigator (isReady() turns true) and otherwise subscribes to the container's `ready` event via `navigationRef.current?.addListener('ready')`. The `onReady` prop was deliberately NOT used because __tests__/wf/be-mobile-security-secrets.test.ts pins the literal `<NavigationContainer ref={navigationRef} theme={theme}>` (linking-free container proof) and out-of-scope test mocks of createNavigationContainerRef expose only isReady/navigate.
